full_translation: In ancient days, there lived a humble father, mother, and their devoted young son. The young son was virtuous and listened obediently to the Dhamma teachings of the Buddhist monks. One morning while walking along the Buridihing river, he found a golden peacock trapped in a cruel snare. With great compassion, the boy drew his knife, cut the hunter's ropes, and set the magnificent bird free. The golden peacock bowed gracefully and said: 'I offer my deepest gratitude to you, noble youth!' The peacock plucked a shimmering golden feather from its wing and gifted it to the boy. Sometime later, his elderly parents fell gravely ill with a burning jungle fever. The village healers were helpless and declared that no forest herbs could save them. Remembering the peacock's gift, the son dipped the golden feather into a bowl of pure water. The water turned into a luminous healing elixir; upon drinking it, his parents were instantly restored to health. All the villagers of Powaimukh proclaimed: 'Loving-kindness (Metta) conquers all mortal perils.' Thus the traditional Lik Pung stories teach us to walk steadfastly in truth, compassion, and virtue.
